title: Multi-zone disaster-tolerant private control plane: design & operational playbook
author: Jordan Miller
body:
Summary

This document describes a recommended multi-zone, disaster-tolerant architecture for Redwood private control planes (VPC and on‑prem variants) and provides a detailed operational playbook for deployments, upgrades, failover, and day‑2 activities. The guidance focuses on minimizing recovery time (RTO) and limiting data exposure during zone and region faults while preserving predictable inference latency for customer workloads.

Goals
- Provide a repeatable reference architecture for private control plane deployments that must tolerate single-zone and multi-zone failures.
- Define clear upgrade and rollback procedures that avoid split-brain and ensure data consistency across control-plane replicas.
- Offer runbooks for the most likely operational incidents (zone outage, control-plane quorum loss, disk failure, and partial network partitions).
- Specify hardware/network and observability requirements needed for SLAs and safe failovers.

Non-goals
- This is not a full OPA or IAM policy manual; it references security controls but does not re-specify them.
- It does not replace customer-specific compliance work (SOC2/HIPAA) required for Private on‑prem certification.

Architecture overview

High level: a three-tier control-plane design distributed across at least three failure domains (AZs or data‑center racks). Primary service components are: Control API (stateless), Metadata store (strongly-consistent replicated datastore), Scheduler/orchestrator, Telemetry/metrics aggregator, and Storage for small persistent state (e.g., keys, pointers).

Diagram (text):
- Zone A: API, Scheduler leader candidate, Metrics aggregator replica, Metadata replica (voter)
- Zone B: API, Scheduler follower, Metrics aggregator replica, Metadata replica (voter)
- Zone C: API, Scheduler follower, Metrics aggregator replica, Metadata replica (voter)

Components and requirements
- API tier: 3+ replicas per zone behind a local L4 load balancer. Health checks: /healthz (component), /ready (dependencies).
- Metadata store: etcd or CockroachDB recommended. Configure an odd-numbered quorum (3 or 5) and place voters across zones. Use dedicated NVMe-SSD for DB WAL.
- Scheduler/orchestrator: leader election using metadata store; colocate leader candidates to reduce cross-zone election churn.
- Object storage: customer-managed S3 compatible endpoint (for private on‑prem use minio or Ceph), cross‑region replication optional but recommended for long-term backups.
- Gossip/mesh: control-plane uses mTLS service mesh for control traffic; configure TTLs to tolerate brief network jitter.

Network and security requirements (table)

| Requirement | Recommendation | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Control plane inter-zone bandwidth | >= 500 Mbps per node pair (10 Gbps preferred) | Fast replication and low election latency |
| Control plane latency | < 20 ms typical inter-AZ | Avoid leader elections and maintain KV throughput |
| Firewall rules | Allow ports: 2200 (control agent), 2379-2380 (etcd), 8443 (API), 9090 (metrics) | Restrict to CIDR blocks for control-plane nodes and operator IPs |
| KMS integration | Customer KMS reachable from all zones via private link | Key availability required for startup and encrypted secrets |

Hardware baseline (per control-plane node)
- CPU: 8 vCPU (or equivalent physical cores)
- Memory: 32 GB RAM
- Disk: 1 x 1TB NVMe for DB WAL + 1 x 500GB OS SSD
- Network: 10 Gbps NIC recommended for replication heavy workloads

Deployment topology options
1) Stretched three‑AZ deployment (VPC): keep voters across AZs; latency-sensitive, single-region.
2) Paired-region active/passive: warm standby in secondary region with asynchronous replication — lower RTO for read-only operations, requires cross-region networking and replicated backups.
3) Air-gapped on-prem cluster: three physical racks mapped to failure domains; use dedicated out-of-band management network for operator access.

Bootstrapping and initial deployment steps (numbered)
1. Validate prerequisites (see checklist below).
2. Provision networking: subnets per AZ, private link to KMS, firewall rules for operator CIDRs.
3. Seed metadata store with initial configuration (3 voters) on different AZs/racks.
4. Deploy API tier in each AZ behind local LBs; configure health checks and traffic weights.
5. Start scheduler candidates and confirm leader election stability for 10 minutes.
6. Deploy metrics/observability stack and verify traces show all replicas.
7. Run smoke tests (10k small requests at low concurrency) to validate latency and correctness.

Pre-deploy checklist (bullet list)
- Operator public keys uploaded to each node
- KMS test-signature validated from each zone
- DNS SRV/A records created for control-plane endpoints
- Time sync (NTP/PTP) validated across nodes
- Backups scheduled and snapshot retention policies set

Canary upgrade procedure (safe rollout)
1. Create a canary availability zone (A) traffic weight 0.
2. Apply control-plane upgrade to one API replica in Zone A. Run integration and health checks for 15 minutes.
3. Promote the upgraded API replica to receive 1% traffic; monitor latency, error rate, and metrics (5 min steady-state).
4. Upgrade one metadata voter in Zone A (non-leader) and confirm metadata quorum health.
5. If all checks pass, gradually roll forward across remaining replicas in Zone A, then repeat for Zone B and C.

Upgrade safety gates (abort conditions)
- Error rate > 1% absolute increase for 10 continuous minutes.
- 99th percentile latency degradation > 2x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Metadata store commit failures or dropped quorum.

Rollback procedure (numbered, concise)
1. Immediately divert all new control-plane traffic to a stable zone or dedicated fallback (e.g., read-only fallback cluster).
2. Promote previous stable API binary (keep previous Docker image in registry with immutable tag) and restart API replicas in the affected zone with immutable tags.
3. If metadata schema was migrated in the failed upgrade, restore metadata from the nearest snapshot taken before the upgrade. Follow snapshot restore validation steps (see section below).
4. Run full integration smoke tests and re-enable traffic weightings incrementally.

Snapshot and restore (metadata)
- Snapshot frequency: hourly with 24-hour retention; daily full snapshots with 30-day retention.
- Restore validation: after restore, run the validation script:

```bash
# validate-metadata-restore.sh
curl -sSf https://controlplane.local/healthz || exit 1
# run a set of validation queries that check 50 sample objects
python tools/validate_metadata.py --sample 50
```

Day-2 operations checklist
- Rolling certificate rotation: rotate leaf certs quarterly; rotate CA only via planned maintenance windows.
- Disk pressure handling: set alert at 70% usage; automated ephemeral log rotation and retained 10 days.
- Node replacement: use immutable imaging; prepare replacement node, join to cluster, cordon and drain failed node, decommission via API.
- Capacity scaling: adjust scheduler weights and increase API replicas per zone before scheduling heavy inference migrations.

Runbook: zone failure (rapid)
1. Detect: automatic alert fires when >50% local API endpoints fail health checks or metadata quorum moves.
2. Triage: check cross-zone network connectivity (traceroute) and metadata store leader status.
3. Failover: if quorum intact, divert traffic away from affected AZ via route weights; if quorum lost, promote read-only fallback cluster and notify customers per SLA.
4. Recovery: bring new nodes up in surviving zones and re-balance voters to restore odd quorum where possible.

Runbook: metadata quorum loss (emergency)
1. Immediately isolate actions (no schema migrations, no rollouts).
2. Identify minority/majority voter set. If majority exists, restart failed voters one-by-one ensuring they rejoin the cluster without data divergence.
3. If no majority, restore from most recent consistent snapshot and bring up a 3-voter cluster from snapshot; stop application writes until cluster stable.

Testing and validation
- Annually run a full DR rehearsal: zone failover, metadata restore, and cold-start from snapshot. Record RTO and RPO.
- Run monthly chaos tests: kill a randomly selected control-plane node and verify automatic recovery within 10 minutes.
- Maintain a canary test harness that runs synthetic inference workloads (token distribution similar to customer traffic).

Observability and SLOs
- SLOs: 99.9% control-plane availability per month (excluding planned maintenance), 95th percentile API latency < 120 ms for small requests.
- Key metrics: metadata commit latency, leader election frequency, control-plane CPU/memory, WAL write latency, snapshot duration.
- Alerts (examples): metadata_commit_latency > 500ms for 5m, leader_election_count > 3 in 10m, disk_usage > 85%

Packaging and air-gap notes
- Produce an OCI bundle that contains: control-plane images (immutable), operator CLI, migration tools, schema snapshots, and offline KMS hooks. Include a SHA256 manifest and signed release notes.
- For air-gapped installs: provide a bootstrap ISO with pre-seeded metadata snapshot and a verification script for images (cosign or sigstore recommended).

Operational ownership and contacts
- Ownership: eng-private-deployments (primary), eng-sre (pager duty during incidents), eng-serving-runtime (for runtime compatibility).
- Escalation: Primary oncall -> Senior Platform Engineer -> Head of SRE. Maintain a 24/7 oncall rota for production incidents.

Appendices
A. Example etcd YAML config snippet:

```yaml
# /etc/etcd/etcd.conf.yaml
name: "cp-node-1"
initial-advertise-peer-urls: "https://10.0.0.11:2380"
listen-peer-urls: "https://0.0.0.0:2380"
listen-client-urls: "https://0.0.0.0:2379"
initial-cluster-token: "redwood-cp-cluster-2026"
initial-cluster: "cp-node-1=https://10.0.0.11:2380,cp-node-2=https://10.0.1.11:2380,cp-node-3=https://10.0.2.11:2380"
initial-cluster-state: "new"
```

B. Quick validation commands:
- Check leader: curl -sSf https://controlplane.local/leader | jq .
- Check quorum: etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.0.0.11:2379 member list

References and related documents
- See hybrid-control-plane-reference-architecture for hybrid routing notes.
- See day-2-ops/chaos-drills for rehearsal checklists.
